commits.message:
refactor(segment): two bounding primitives, named; Table splits through the one (rich-segment-bpa)

cropLines keeps a stream's line structure and bounds it; splitAndCropLines
decomposes into rows of exactly the width. segment.ts now says which question
each answers. Table's hand-rolled splitLines+adjustLineLength is the second
one, so it calls it. splitAndCropLines' pad/includeNewLines/style modes had no
caller and are gone.

feat(widgets): hit-test the painted frame; widgets get their own coordinates (rich-runtime-fna.2)

WidgetBase.render stamps a subclass's `draw` output with its anchor, so the
frame a screen paints is its own hit map. `widgetAt(frame, x, y)` names the
innermost widget under a cell and the cell's place in that widget's output;
EventRouter reads it off `FrameSource.frame` and delivers each pointer event
in the widget's own coordinates, a captured drag relative to the origin its
press found. `bounds`, `WidgetBounds`, `containsPoint`, the active-overlay
set and the z-sorted `widgets` getter are gone: z-order is paint order, and
the overlay pass stamps overlay row i as the widget's row footprint+i.

feat(core): a cell carries where its owner drew it (rich-runtime-fna.1) (#191)

* feat(core): a cell carries where its owner drew it, so a nested widget's position is read off the frame (rich-runtime-fna.1)

The design answer for the composed runtime, landed as its contract rather
than a design document, as rich-viewport-owi.1 did. An origin threaded down
the render options cannot exist: Align places each line after rendering it,
so one widget's rows start at different columns. Position travels up
instead: `Anchor` rides on each segment's Style, which every container
already preserves, and `Segment.anchorAt` reads any cell of a composed
frame. test/core/anchor.test.ts proves it through every container.

The remaining answers are on rich-runtime-fna.2, .3, .4 and
rich-viewport-owi.5.

* fix(core): anchors stay true through wide-glyph cuts and RichText; Style copies share one field list (rich-runtime-fna.1)

Review (high) of #191:
- splitCells shifts the right half by the cells it gave up (len - cellLen(right)),
  not leftText's width, which splitText pads when the cut lands mid-glyph.
- anchorAt answers undefined for a non-cell x (negative, fractional), as it
  already did for y; it shifts the anchor directly instead of building a Style.
- RichText admits no anchor (admitStyle): it lays text out anew, so a stamp
  from the output it came from would name the wrong cell.
- Style's four hand-copied clones go through one private with(); the
  optionless constructor branch folds into a default.
- Anchor is exported from the barrel beside the Style/Segment surface that
  names it.
